title: Proper base change for arbitrary etale sheaves of sets on algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaves of sets on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and the canonical inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions and composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model, lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism]. Let $f:Y\to Z$ be proper [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], let $g:Z'\to Z$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces, and put $Y'=Y\times_Z Z'$ with projections $f':Y'\to Z'$ and $g':Y'\to Y$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every sheaf of sets $F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, the canonical base-change map
$$g^{-1}f_*F\longrightarrow f'_*g'^{-1}F$$
is an isomorphism. Here the map is the adjoint under $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ of
$$f'^{-1}g^{-1}f_*F\simeq g'^{-1}f^{-1}f_*F\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}\epsilon_f}g'^{-1}F,$$
where $\epsilon_f$ is the adjunction counit. The isomorphism is natural in $F$. No surjectivity, finite-presentation, Noetherianity, representability, group structure, or torsion hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DG0 (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), full statement and proof. Canonical mate normalization is the base-change map used there; compare etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star).

proof.text: Work on the enlarged sites of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Along an etale map inverse image is restriction to the localized site; direct image evaluates on fibre products by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism]. Thus etale restriction of either side of the asserted map is the corresponding side for the restricted square; its adjoint is still the restricted counit. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $V\to Z$ and then a surjective etale scheme chart $V_1\to V\times_ZZ'$, using [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. It suffices to prove the result for the pulled-back square with base map $V_1\to V$. Indeed, on every test object its inverse image along these covers is a bijection; local inverse sections agree on overlaps by injectivity and glue uniquely by the sheaf axiom. Refine $V$ by affine opens, then refine their inverse images in $V_1$ by affine opens. This reduces to $Z$ and $Z'$ affine, without assuming $g$ etale. The restricted vertical morphisms remain proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0DG0 (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), proof, first paragraph, etale and Zariski localization

proof.text: Now $Z$ is affine and $f:Y\to Z$ is separated of finite type. Regard these spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers], which preserves fibre products, small etale sites and maps to $S$, so that a scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with a map to $Y$ is again a scheme over $S$, and apply [lem-sfb-space-weak-chow] to obtain a universally surjective proper map $h_1:Y_1\to Y$ from a scheme. Put $Y_2=Y_1\times_YY_1$, with projections $r_1,r_2$, and $h_2=h_1r_1=h_1r_2$. This is a scheme: it is the pullback of the representable diagonal of $Y$ along the scheme $Y_1\times_SY_1$, by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Each $r_i$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change], so $h_2$ and $k_i=fh_i:Y_i\to Z$ are proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition]. These applications require only separated finite type and properness, with no finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0DG0 (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), proof, second paragraph, weak Chow cover and its double overlap

proof.text: Write $Y_i'=Y_i\times_ZZ'$, $v_i:Y_i'\to Y_i$, $h_i':Y_i'\to Y'$, and $k_i'=f' h_i'$. The schemes $Y_i'$ are also $Y_i\times_YY'$, and $Y_2'=Y_1'\times_{Y'}Y_1'$, by the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The map $h_1'$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] and surjective by the universal surjectivity in [lem-sfb-space-weak-chow]. Put $F_i=h_i^{-1}F$ and $F'=g'^{-1}F$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-surjection-set-sheaf-equalizer] to $h_1,F$ and $h_1',F'$. It gives $F=\operatorname{Eq}(h_{1,*}F_1\rightrightarrows h_{2,*}F_2)$ and $F'=\operatorname{Eq}(h_{1,*}' v_1^{-1}F_1\rightrightarrows h_{2,*}' v_2^{-1}F_2)$, with the specified projection-unit arrows.

source.place: Tag 0DG0 (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), proof, equalizer diagrams before and after base change

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] these equalizers are sectionwise. The direct-image formula of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] therefore shows that $f_*$ and $f'_*$ preserve them; that node also says that $g^{-1}$ is left exact. Consequently the source and target of the asserted map are respectively the equalizers of
$$g^{-1}k_{1,*}F_1\rightrightarrows g^{-1}k_{2,*}F_2,\qquad k_{1,*}' v_1^{-1}F_1\rightrightarrows k_{2,*}' v_2^{-1}F_2.$$
For $i=1,2$ apply [lem-sfb-scheme-proper-set-sheaf-base-change] to the proper scheme morphism $k_i$, arbitrary scheme map $g$, and set sheaf $F_i$. It gives isomorphisms $b_i:g^{-1}k_{i,*}F_i\simeq k_{i,*}' v_i^{-1}F_i$.

source.place: Tag 0DG0 (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), proof, scheme base change on the two terms, and preservation of equalizers

proof.text: Check the arrows using the adjunctions and composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model, lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism]. For a projection $r:Y_2\to Y_1$, its arrow is $k_{1,*}\eta_r$ followed by $r^{-1}F_1=F_2$. A base-change mate is obtained by applying the horizontal pullback to the vertical counit. Expand the composite units and counits as $\eta_{ab}=\eta_a;a_*\eta_b a^{-1}$ and $\epsilon_{ab}=b^{-1}\epsilon_a b_*;\epsilon_b$ for composable maps $b$ then $a$. Naturality of $\eta_r$ moves it past the counit, and $r_*\epsilon_r\circ\eta_r r_*=1$ cancels the adjacent pair. This proves $b_2\circ g^{-1}(k_{1,*}\eta_r)=(k_{1,*}'\eta_{r'})\circ b_1$, for both projections. The same expansion with $h_i$ shows that the mate $\beta:g^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*g'^{-1}F$ commutes with the equalizer inclusions: the composite counit for $fh_i$ is $h_i^{-1}\epsilon_f h_{i,*};\epsilon_{h_i}$. Thus the induced map of equalizers is exactly the counit mate in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0DG0 (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), proof, details omitted: compatibility of projection units and canonical counit mates

proof.text: An isomorphism between the two parallel-arrow diagrams induces a bijection between their equalizers: send a matching section by $b_1$; the commutative squares show that it matches, and $b_1^{-1}$ gives the inverse since $b_2$ is invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], $\beta$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. The counit and all composition comparisons are natural in $F$ by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], so the isomorphism is natural. If $Y$ or $Z'$ is empty, the same equalizer and restriction argument applies to the unique sheaf on the empty site. No point, group operation, or torsion restriction was used.
